newsitem.title: USA: Apria to cut non-core services by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Apria to cut non-core services by year-end.

text.p: Apria Healthcare Group Inc said Tuesday that it plans to cut back non-core services by the end of the year.
The company announced a second-quarter net loss of $69.9 million, or $1.36 per share versus net income of $21.9 million, or $0.42 per share, for the same period last year.
The net loss for the quarter was due to charges and write-offs totaling $98 million, it said.

The company Tuesday said second quarter results were consistent with the company's announcement last month that it intended to report charges relating to accounts receivable, inventory and efforts to restructure its operations to focus on core business lines of respiratory services, infusion therapy and home medical equipment.

Apria's said its efforts to emphasize its three primary business lines are also on track, and the company is proceeding with plans to eliminate or reduce lower- margin, non-core offerings, such as subcontracted home health nursing and medical supply sales, by year-end 1997.

"We believe that our heightened focus on Apria's core services, along with a continued commitment of resources to reduce accounts receivable, will position the company for improved performance in the future," said chief executive Jeremy Jones.
